This document provides an introduction to AgentScope, its design philosophy, core capabilities, and high-level architecture. It serves as an entry point for understanding how the framework's major subsystems work together to enable the development of production-ready agentic applications.

For installation instructions and initial setup, see Installation and Setup. For detailed architectural concepts, see Core Concepts and Architecture.

Sources: README.md58-65 README_zh.md58-65

What is AgentScope?

AgentScope is a production-ready agent framework that provides flexible abstractions designed to work with evolving large language model capabilities. The framework includes built-in support for model finetuning and emphasizes leveraging models' native reasoning and tool-use abilities rather than constraining them with rigid prompt engineering or opinionated orchestrations.

The current version is 1.0.16dev, requiring Python 3.10 or higher.

Key Design Principles:

PrincipleDescription
SimpleBuild agents in minutes with built-in ReActAgent, tools, memory, planning, and evaluation
ExtensibleLarge ecosystem integrations for tools, memory, observability; native MCP and A2A protocol support
Production-readyDeploy locally, serverless, or on K8s with built-in OpenTelemetry observability

Sources: README.md58-71 src/agentscope/_version.py1-4

Design Philosophy

AgentScope is designed for increasingly agentic LLMs. The framework's approach prioritizes:

  1. Model-Driven Reasoning: Leverage models' native reasoning capabilities rather than imposing fixed workflows
  2. Flexible Tool Integration: Enable dynamic tool use through Toolkit with middleware support, rather than hardcoded function chains
  3. Adaptive Memory: Provide multi-tiered memory (short-term, long-term, knowledge bases) that adapts to context needs
  4. Observable Execution: Built-in OpenTelemetry tracing for all components without code changes
  5. Production Deployment: First-class support for distributed deployment and state management

This philosophy manifests in the framework's core abstraction: the ReActAgent, which orchestrates reasoning and action cycles rather than following predefined state machines.

High-Level Architecture

AgentScope's architecture consists of seven major subsystems that interact through well-defined interfaces. The following diagram shows how these systems relate to core code entities:

Sources: README.md72-77

Major Subsystems

1. Core Agent Framework

The foundation of AgentScope applications. Key classes:

  • AgentBase: Abstract base class defining the agent interface with reply() method
  • ReActAgent: Primary built-in agent implementing Reasoning-Acting paradigm
  • UserAgent: Handles human-in-the-loop interactions
  • MsgHub: Manages multi-agent coordination with participant management
  • PlanNotebook: Provides task decomposition and planning capabilities

For details, see Agent System.

Sources: README.md172-210

2. Model Integration Layer

Unified abstraction for multiple LLM providers:

  • ChatModelBase: Abstract interface all models implement
  • Provider implementations: OpenAIChatModel, DashScopeChatModel, AnthropicChatModel, GeminiChatModel, OllamaChatModel
  • FormatterBase: Converts internal Msg objects to provider-specific formats
  • ChatResponse: Standardized response containing ContentBlock unions (text, thinking, tool calls, media)

Enables provider switching with minimal code changes. For details, see Model Integration.

Sources: README.md186-198

3. Tool System

Extensible tool management and execution:

  • Toolkit: Central registry for tool functions with JSON schema generation
  • Tool sources: Python functions, MCP services, agent skills
  • Middleware system: Onion model for pre/post-processing (logging, auth, transforms)
  • Tool groups: Dynamic activation/deactivation of tool subsets
  • reset_equipped_tools: Meta-tool for runtime tool management

For details, see Tool System.

Sources: README.md184-186 README.md238-268

4. Memory & State Management

Multi-tiered memory architecture:

  • Short-term (Working) Memory: InMemoryMemory, RedisMemory, AsyncSQLAlchemyMemory
    • Message marks for filtering
    • LLM-based compression with CompressionConfig
  • Long-term Memory: Mem0LongTermMemory with semantic storage via mem0 library
  • Session Management: JSONSession, RedisSession for checkpoint/restore via StateModule protocol

For details, see Memory and Knowledge Systems.

Sources: README.md84

5. RAG & Knowledge System

Document retrieval and semantic search:

  • Document ingestion: Specialized readers (PDFReader, WordReader, ExcelReader, etc.)
  • Embedding generation: EmbeddingModelBase with provider implementations
  • Vector stores: QdrantStore, MilvusLiteStore, OceanBaseStore, MongoDBStore
  • KnowledgeBase: High-level interface coordinating retrieval pipeline

For details, see RAG System Overview.

Sources: README.md324-330

6. Observability

Built-in OpenTelemetry tracing:

  • Decorators: @trace_llm, @trace_reply, @trace_format, @trace_toolkit, @trace
  • Backends: AgentScope Studio (native), or third-party (CloudMonitor, Phoenix, Langfuse)
  • Exporters: OTLP HTTP/gRPC
  • Automatic span management with attributes for inputs, outputs, errors

For details, see Observability and Tracing.

Sources: docs/tutorial/en/src/task_tracing.py8-14 docs/tutorial/zh_CN/src/task_tracing.py8-14

7. Evaluation System

Quality assessment and benchmarking:

  • OpenJudge integration: Adapter for graders (RelevanceGrader, CorrectnessGrader)
  • Benchmark framework: BenchmarkBase, Task, MetricResult
  • Custom metrics: Extensible evaluation infrastructure

For details, see Evaluation System.

Sources: README.md356-360

Core Message Protocol

AgentScope uses the Msg class as the fundamental unit of communication between agents and components. Messages contain:

  • name: Sender identifier
  • content: Content blocks (text, tool use, thinking, media)
  • role: Message role ("system", "user", "assistant")
  • metadata: Additional context and attributes

Content blocks are typed unions enabling multimodal interactions and structured tool interactions.

For details, see Message Protocol and Content Blocks.

ModelsChatModelBaseNew LLM provider integrations
FormattersFormatterBaseProvider-specific message formatting

MemoryMemoryBaseAlternative storage backends
LTMLongTermMemoryBaseCustom long-term memory systems
Vector StoresVDBStoreBaseNew vector database integrations

Getting Started

To begin building with AgentScope:

  1. Install: pip install agentscope or from source
  2. Initialize: Call agentscope.init() with optional observability configuration
  3. Create Agent: Instantiate ReActAgent with model, memory, and toolkit
  4. Run: Call agent with messages in an async loop

See Installation and Setup for detailed instructions and Core Concepts and Architecture for fundamental concepts.
